form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Scott of Florida, under authority of the order of the Senate of September 30, 2026, introduced the following bill; which was ordered read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs

form.official-title: To require the debarment of any Federal contractor who improperly discloses personally identifiable information, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the No Cash for Incompetent and Malicious Contractors Act.

section.header: Debarment of contractors who improperly disclose personally identifiable information

subsection.text: Chapter 47 of title 41, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

section.header: Debarment of contractors who improperly disclose personally identifiable information

subsection.header: Debarment for legal finding of improper disclosure

paragraph.text: The head of an executive agency shall debar a contractor from eligibility for Federal contracts for a conviction or civil judgment against the contractor, or an employee of the contractor, for non-consensual disclosure of personally identifiable information of a client of the contractor, including with respect to the client—

subparagraph.text: return or return information, as defined in paragraphs (1) and (2) of section 6103(b) of title 26;
individually identifiable health information, as defined in section 160.103 of title 45, Code of Federal Regulations, or any successor regulation; or
any trade secret, as defined in section 1839 of title 18.

paragraph.text: A debarment under paragraph (1) shall be for a period of not less than one year and not more than 5 years, dependent on the severity of the conduct.
A debarment under paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with the procedural requirements of section 9.406–3 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation, or any successor regulation.

subsection.header: Suspension pending investigation of improper disclosure

paragraph.text: The head of an executive agency shall suspend a contractor from eligibility for Federal contracts if the contractor, or an employee of the contractor, is charged with commission of a criminal offense involving disclosure of personally identifiable information of a client of the contractor, including the information listed in subparagraphs (A) through (D) of subsection (a)(1).
A suspension under paragraph (1) shall be for the period prescribed in section 9.407–4 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation, or any successor regulation.
A suspension under paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with the procedural requirements of section 9.407–3 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation, or any successor regulation.

subsection.text: The table of contents at the beginning of chapter 47 of title 41, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

toc.toc-entry: Sec. 4715. Debarment of contractors who improperly disclose personally identifiable information.
